subject: Coordinated renewal plan: GitHub / JetBrains / Atlassian
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Coordinated renewal plan: GitHub / JetBrains / Atlassian

Team —

Our GitHub Enterprise, JetBrains and Atlassian renewals are clustered in Q4 and I want to propose we coordinate negotiation and PO timing to maximize combined discounts and reduce procurement overhead. High-level asks: 

- Laura: can you pull the latest quotes and confirm renewal windows / early-terminate penalties?
- Marcus & Dev: please confirm active seat counts (engineering + infra + data) and any seat reductions expected in H1 2027.
- Rachel: what’s the latest PO timeline we should target for Finance to approve consolidated deals (monthly cut-off / approvals)?

I attached current_license_inventory.csv for quick reference. My proposal is to run a single negotiation bundle and sign separate vendor agreements but with simultaneous effective dates — that helped us last time with billing alignment.

If we can lock decisions by 2026-12-10 we have space for review and signatures before year-end.

Thanks —
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, IT Procurement
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Dec 2026 11:30:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Coordinated renewal plan: GitHub / JetBrains / Atlassian

Hannah —

Thanks for the heads-up. I pulled preliminary vendor materials and attached two files: GitHub_quote_Q4_2026.pdf and Atlassian_pricing_2027.xlsx. Quick notes: 

- GitHub: renewal window opens 2026-12-20. Current committed seats on the enterprise billing account: 280 active seats, 15 suspended seats. Vendor rep said a multi-product consolidation may qualify for a combined discount but needs firm counts.
- Atlassian: renewal is on a calendar-year plan; our Jira/Confluence bill runs 2027-01-15. They offered a 12-month price hold if we sign by 2026-12-17.
- JetBrains: Elena asked for a usage snapshot (active IDs) and whether we want floating vs named licences — she’s open to a term license consolidation.

Procurement questions: which legal entity should be billed for each vendor? Historically GitHub and JetBrains have been billed to Redwood Inc (US), Atlassian was routed through the EU billing account. If we want single fiscal alignment we may need to switch billing entity which can delay the process ~3 business days.

Next steps: please confirm seat counts and preferred billing entity. I’ll request combined discount proposals once we have the counts and agree the billing approach.

Laura Bennett
Senior Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: GitHub_quote_Q4_2026.pdf, Atlassian_pricing_2027.xlsx
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Dec 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Coordinated renewal plan: GitHub / JetBrains / Atlassian

Hannah / Laura —

Seat counts (as of 2026-12-01):
- Engineering: 180 active GitHub seats; 6 infra/service accounts (license-exempt).
- Data & AI: 60 active seats (mix of engineers and research).
- Platform & Security: 40 seats (includes automation bots on enterprise account).

Total active GitHub seats I see: 280 (matches procurement). We don’t expect major headcount cuts in Q1 2027, but we will convert ~10 contractors to full-time in Jan which may increase seats by ~10. Recommend we purchase a 300-seat block to avoid mid-term add-ons and get better per-seat pricing.

JetBrains: roughly 210 active users across IntelliJ / PyCharm / TeamCity plugins. We have ~25 users who only use the free community editions and can be de-scoped. Dev recommends named licenses for consistent seat assignment (easier for audit), but floating could shave 10% off cost if we accept occasional contention.

SSO note: we’ll need a short maintenance window if vendor requires SAML reconfiguration — plan for a 2-hr window in the mid-morning to avoid disruptions.

Marcus
Engineering Manager, Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Dec 2026 10:05:14 -0800
Subject: Re: Coordinated renewal plan: GitHub / JetBrains / Atlassian

Quick add — JetBrains usage snapshot attached. A couple operational suggestions: 

- Move to JetBrains All-Products Pack for dev tooling teams that use multiple IDEs; simplifies license management and usually results in better overall cost per user.
- Reclaim stale JetBrains licenses: I’ll run an offboarding sweep to free up ~15 seats before we purchase.
- For Atlassian, consider moving lower-use Confluence spaces to view-only to reduce user tier counts.

I’ll coordinate with SRE on the SAML maintenance window Marcus mentioned.

—Dev
Staff Software Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: jetbrains_usage_snapshot.png
From: Samir Kapoor <skapoor@github.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 14:20:05 -0800
Subject: Re: Coordinated renewal plan: GitHub / JetBrains / Atlassian — preliminary bundle pricing

Hi Hannah / Laura —

Thanks for the details. Based on the 300-seat ask and inclusion of the Atlassian bundle, GitHub can offer a combined negotiation credit of 18% off our standard enterprise seat rate if agreements are executed within the same 30-day window. Highlights: 

- Proposed license block: 300 seats, 12-month term, annual billing.
- Combined negotiation credit: 18% applied to GitHub line items if we sign within the coordinated window.
- DocuSign link to preliminary SOW attached: https://go.docusign.com/Signing/?env=prod&token=ABCD1234

I’m available for a 30-minute call Monday (2026-12-07) to finalize quant and timeline. If you’d like, I can pull a formal price stack showing per-seat math vs add-ons.

Best regards,
Samir Kapoor
Enterprise Sales — GitHub
skapoor@github.com
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Coordinated renewal plan: GitHub / JetBrains / Atlassian

Thanks everyone — good progress. Quick summary and next steps: 

- Seat counts confirmed: GitHub 300 (purchase block), JetBrains ~195-200 after reclaim sweep, Atlassian TBD but likely within current band.
- Procurement (Laura): please request formal combined discount proposals from each vendor and hold the DocuSign windows aligned (target sign-by: 2026-12-17).
- Finance (Rachel): can you confirm PO approval timeline? We’re aiming for a consolidated PO package under PO-2026-1177.
- Ops (Marcus & Dev): schedule a 2-hr SSO maintenance window with SRE; we’ll coordinate with vendor onboarding teams for any SAML changes.

Related items: Jira ticket created to track procurement steps: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PROC-4721. Laura — please attach the vendor quotes to the Jira ticket.

If nobody objects I’ll lock dates and run the combined negotiation call. Need final confirmation by 2026-12-10 so Procurement has time to negotiate and Finance can route signatures.

Thanks —
Hannah
Director, IT Procurement
Redwood Inference
